subject: When are cache hits billed? + trial/commit proposal
messages:
From: Jun Sato <j.sato@olympus.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@olympus.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on prefix cache billing + trial credits

Hi Mina —

We're kicking off a scoped pilot of an assistant that relies heavily on template prefixes and session state (conversation history + a 1200-token system template). Before we finalize the PoC cadence, procurement asked for a plain-English explanation of how Redwood bills when "prefix" or "prompt-state" is served from cache. Two quick scenarios we need clarity on: 

1) Full cache hit: the stored prefix + completion is returned without invoking the model (same model version, same generation params). Is Olympus charged for any tokens in that case?

2) Partial hit: the cached prefix is used but the model must generate the rest of the response (e.g., cached first 300 tokens of a 900-token reply). How are input and output tokens billed?

Also can you attach the hosted API rate card and confirm if Redwood offers any temporary credits for cache-heavy experiments (we expect most of our traffic to be repeating prefixes during the pilot).

Thanks — appreciate a short breakdown we can share with procurement.

— Jun
Jun Sato
Head of Product, Olympus AI
procurement@olympus.ai

(Attachment: session-logs-snippet.txt)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on prefix cache billing + trial credits

Hi Jun —

Thanks for the clear scenarios. Short answers up front, then a couple of concrete examples. I've attached our May 2027 hosted ratecard as well.

Summary: 
- Full cache hit: you are NOT charged the standard model generation compute for the cached portion. Instead, a small cache-retrieval fee applies per request (see ratecard line: "prefix-lookup request fee"). No output generation tokens are billed because the model didn't run to produce them.
- Partial cache hit: we apply the cache-retrieval fee for the request + regular token charges for any tokens the model actually generates beyond the cached prefix. Input tokens that are part of the cached prefix are treated as cached tokens and are not charged at the full input-token rate; instead they contribute only to the cache-storage & lookup billing (covered in the lookup fee).

Concrete examples (hosted API):
- Example A (full hit): Client request equals stored prefix + stored completion; cache returns the completion. Billing: 1 x prefix-lookup fee (flat), NO generation token charges.
- Example B (partial hit): Stored prefix = 300 tokens, model must generate 600 additional tokens. Billing: 1 x prefix-lookup fee + generation charges for 600 output tokens (standard per-token rate).

Notes/constraints: 
- Cache hits are only eligible when model version, sampling parameters (temperature/top_p), and prompt normalization match. Minor parameter changes force a miss and full generation.
- TTL / eviction: cached prefixes expire based on storage retention in the ratecard (default 30d for pilot). Longer retention is available as an add-on.

Credit/discount options: we can extend a short-term trial credit specifically to offset lookup fees for pilot traffic, and provide a starter committed discount if Olympus signs a 12-month committed spend. Ben is cc'd to propose numbers.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-may2027.xlsx (contains the lookup fee, per-token rates, and retention add-ons).

If you want, I can turn the examples above into a one-page note for procurement.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Thanks Mina — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups so procurement can sign off: 

A) For partial hits, do you count the cached prefix tokens at all toward any input token quota or is it effectively free aside from the lookup fee? Procurement is parsing "not charged the standard model generation compute" vs. whether input-token metering still applies.

B) We do a lot of session-affinity where we stitch short user messages onto a long (1k–1.2k) system template. If that system template is cached, will every request that reuses it (but has a unique user message) qualify as a hit?

C) Can you confirm limits on cache lookups per second for hosted customers (just need an expected throughput number).

If it's easier, Ben or Marissa can share a short example from our pilot traffic and you can map it to the ratecard.

— Jun

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@olympus.ai
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on prefix cache billing + trial credits

Hi Jun — following up with more precise wording so procurement has something verbatim to include in their SOW. Answers below: 

A) Partial hits and input-token accounting: For hosted API billing we separate two concerns — (1) model compute (generation) and (2) cache/storage & lookup. When a prefix is served from cache: 
  - The cached portion is NOT billed as model generation tokens.
  - The cached portion is also NOT billed at the standard input-token rate. Instead, the per-request prefix-lookup fee covers retrieval and metadata accounting. There is no double-counting of those tokens.

B) Re: session-affinity + variable user messages: A cached system template qualifies as a hit only if the exact normalized bytes of the prefix (system template + any leading context you choose to store) match the cache key for the request. That means differing user messages appended after the cached prefix do not invalidate the hit — as long as the cached portion is the same and the model params match. In practice teams keep one canonical system template as a cached prefix and send the per-user content as dynamic input; that is a common and supported pattern.

C) Throughput/quotas: Hosted lookup throughput defaults to 150 lookups/sec per account, with burst to 500/s for pilot customers. If you need sustained higher throughput we'll include a dedicated lookup tier in the Dedicated plan (Ben can share numbers).

If that language looks good, Ben and I will follow-up with a short pilot commercial: 90 days of lookup-fee credits up to $3,000 and a starter 12-month commit discount (15% off list) if Olympus commits $50k ARR. Marissa — if this matches our standard pilot playbook please flag any compliance notes.

Best,
Mina
